# PassGate
> PassGate is a passkey (WebAuthn) implementation kit for SaaS teams that want passwordless sign-in: a $49 template pack or a $299 done-for-you install with a 48-hour delivery window. It is implementation help, not a security audit.

- Home: https://passgate.incidental.site/
- Template pack: https://passgate.incidental.site/template
- Checklist sample: https://passgate.incidental.site/samples/CHECKLIST.md
- Languages: en (default), zh-CN, zh-TW, ja, ko, ms, vi, fr, es, de — append ?lang=<code>
- Full text: https://passgate.incidental.site/llms-full.txt
- Sitemap: https://passgate.incidental.site/sitemap.xml
- Publisher: Incidental AI (https://incidental.site/)

## Page copy (English)
- Add passkeys to your SaaS in 48 hours
- Ship passwordless login with a DIY template ($49) or book a fixed-fee install ($299). Recovery codes, browser matrix, and a PR you can merge.
- Checkout opens soon via Creem. Nothing is charged yet.
- Demo specimen — not a live auth endpoint
- 2 passkeys · Face ID · security key
- Reset tickets are silent burn
- Every password reset costs support time and some users never come back. Passkeys turn the loop into one device prompt.
- Phishing-resistant by design
- WebAuthn binds each credential to your RP ID, so a look-alike domain cannot use it. Stolen passwords stop being the default way in.
- OS-level UX users already know
- iOS, Android, Windows and macOS already prompt for Face ID, fingerprint, PIN or a security key. Your users have seen it before.
- Click through the three screens the template ships: sign up, save a passkey, manage keys.
- Email only, no password field
- The OS asks for Face ID, fingerprint or PIN
- List, rename and revoke per device
- No password to choose, store or reset.
- Save a passkey for demo.passgate.local?
- Your device asks for Face ID, fingerprint or screen lock. The private key never leaves it.

- What if my repo access is delayed?

- Do you handle Safari autofill quirks?
- Yes, within the web browser matrix in TEST_PLAN. Native app SDKs are out of scope.
- Can I upgrade from template to install?
- Yes. Template buyers can book an install. The $49 is not deducted unless a promotion says so.
- PassGate does not provide a security audit, penetration test or compliance certification (SOC 2, ISO, etc.). You remain responsible for production configuration, RP ID, secret handling and release decisions. Each order documents what is in and out of scope.

- Open any item to see its purpose and a short excerpt. Code blocks have a copy button.
- Runnable Next.js App Router example
- A small Next.js app you can run locally and copy from: sign-up with a passkey, sign-in, a settings page to list and revoke keys, and recovery codes. Server code uses @simplewebauthn/server; the browser side uses @simplewebauthn/browser.
- Route handlers for registration and authentication options + verification
- Challenge store with expiry, plus a session cookie after login
- Settings screen: list, rename, revoke passkeys
- Recovery codes: generate, hash, show once, redeem
- Illustrative HTML render of the example app's settings screen, not a product screenshot.
- Password → passkey migration for Supabase
- Steps for adding passkeys next to existing Supabase password accounts, so current users keep working while they enrol a passkey.
- Create the passkeys table with row-level security
- Offer "add a passkey" after a normal password login
- Let enrolled users sign in with a passkey first, password as fallback
- Optionally hide the password field once a user has two passkeys
- Keep Clerk or move out: a decision note
- If you already use Clerk, this note helps you decide whether to keep it and turn on its passkey option, or move auth into your own database.
- its built-in passkey option covers what you need
- you rely on its user and organisation management UI
- you must own the credential table and session format
- pricing per active user no longer fits your plan
- Thirty checks to run before you turn passkeys on in production, grouped by config, ceremony, storage, UX, recovery and operations.
